title: A Fractured Sanctuary
subtitle: Legends say those stone statues come to life at night.

trails.title: Researchers
trails.description: These researchers consistently exceed all expectations.

content.text:
It was during the Merovingian dynasty that the Bishop of Rouen successfully subdued the first known Gargoyle. This Gargoyle and his descendants then formed a unique lineage devoted to protecting churches across generations. However, in recent times, many younger Gargoyles have chosen to abandon this ancient tradition, leaving their dark church perches for the light and glamour of the modern world.

Based on my recent observations, this generational conflict continues to cause significant distress among elder Gargoyles.
* It's worth noting that the younger generation's departure also relates to modern churches being unable to provide adequate sustenance, reflecting broader societal changes. This aspect warrants further historical analysis.

Gargoyles have some unique arcane skills. First, their arcane ability allows them to petrify their own body parts—a formidable defensive mechanism during the age of close-quarters combat with bayonets and spears, though considerably less effective against modern artillery bombardments.
Additionally, Gargoyles possess exceptional visual capabilities, with particularly remarkable night vision. This trait complements their natural stealth abilities, enabling them to both detect hidden threats with ease and execute perfectly timed ambushes.
* I must admit, it's surprising such impressive combat abilities were historically limited to the protection of churches—though my lack of religious knowledge may explain this confusion.
· Your theological ignorance is indeed astounding. Mandatory religious studies await you.
* While I object to you reading my research notes without permission, I'll concede that compared to your piety, I'm clearly the irreligious one—just a pure biologist.
· Who said I'm not a "pure biologist"?

Gargoyles carry a curse. While the origins of their curse remain shrouded in secrecy, people are open about its manifestations: excessive bloodshed appears to corrupt them. This corruption takes the form of mental instability, progressing from rejecting to completely abandoning their faith.
· Well, my "pure biologist" friend, your Gargoyle research now necessitates the very religious study that you say you have no interest in.
* This notebook clearly requires a sturdier lock.

items.text: A Fractured Sanctuary
Office, Safe Zone

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: An armored vehicle?

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: The driver was a Manus. They're not just supplying the war anymore.
There's a pause before the Hawks' leader speaks through the receiver.

items.speaker: Irinei
items.text: What do you think that means, Creius?
Both sides are gathered in the same room, listening to the reports from the front lines.
Creius lets out a soft, rueful chuckle, though he does not let it betray the seriousness of his words.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: That the Manus have decided to build themselves an army.

items.speaker: Irinei
items.text: That seems likely.

items.speaker: Irinei
items.text: In that case, we must prepare immediately for a response. Zeno's main force is still at the eastern front. They won't be able to reinforce us if anything happens here.

items.speaker: Irinei
items.text: The Foundation will need an army of its own.

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: That's completely irresponsible.
A calm voice cuts through the speculation.

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: It will only increase the tension on this front, and it directly violates our peace policy.

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: Manus Vindictae takes in only pure-blooded arcanists. That doesn't make for a large recruitment pool. It won't be much of an army, really.

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: To say nothing of the fact that they lack the organization or discipline that is needed for a true large-scale military operation. Armies need human leadership.

items.speaker: Irinei
items.text: You forgot to take Arcana into consideration, Pedra. You don't know what she can do to her followers with her new power.

items.speaker: Irinei
items.text: Whatever the case, we cannot take anything for granted. The Foundation will need the strength to defend itself from future attacks by the Manus. If we act quickly, we may even get ahead of things.

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: I'd like to see what the Committee will think of this plan. I hope they'll have a better grasp of the consequences.

items.speaker: Irinei
items.text: You're not seeing the board, Pedra.
The communicator struggles to transmit the two leaders' heated exchange.
Creius, on the other end, stays quiet, professional, obedient.
Before long, the mediator takes over the line.

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: We can't rule out the possibility of a large-scale conflict. However, the Committee will maintain its peace policy until we have reliable evidence.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: And if the worst happens?

items.speaker: Constantine
items.text: Then we'll do what we must to survive, even if that means igniting a worldwide war.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: We have arrived.
Gargoyle Monastery

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: I see ...
The glow of arcane skills fades as they approach, revealing their hidden sanctuary.
It is or was an abbey, appropriately gothic, with ornate stone walls rising up to meet the air—its dome long collapsed.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: This monastery ... It's not an arcane creation, is it?

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: No. It has only been enchanted with our arcane skill "Carthusians."

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Beneath its protection, those that dwell here will go unnoticed by any who pass near.
A Gargoyle dressed in friar's robes walks barefoot on the grass. He looks up from his book to meet the new arrivals.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Greetings. I'm Marsha, Investigator of the St. Pavlov Foundation.
The friar nods, offering a smile soft and friendly, then extends a finger and presses it to his lips.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Oh, I see. Have you made a vow of silence?
"Kra-ka—"
The sound of breaking rock draws her eyes away.
Beneath a broken narrow window, a stone statue of a woman begins to stir, its surface softening into flesh.
Her face is marked by twisted sorrow as she walks toward Sentinel with an exaggerated gait.

items.speaker: Female Gargoyle
items.text: Marie, my sweetie, thou hast returned to us again! But oh! Child, thou needest rest.
She just pulls Marianne into a tight embrace and plants a series of deep kisses on her cheeks.
Sentinel endures the affection with as much grit as she did the bullets.

items.speaker: Female Gargoyle
items.text: And this is a friend?
The woman turns to Marsha, her eyes now pooling with greater sadness.

items.speaker: Female Gargoyle
items.text: Oh, poor child.
The hug comes too quick to dodge and too sturdy to resist, pulling Marsha into a breathtaking embrace.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Ugh ...
One second. Two seconds. Three seconds—
The smothering hospitality at last abates, and Marsha takes a deep breath of fresh air, taking in the pleasant scent of grass and wildflowers.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: *panting*

items.speaker: Female Gargoyle
items.text: Our Marie hast ever been tireless in her toils. 'Tis a shame that she never permits us to aid her. Am I truly too aged to be of service?

items.speaker: Female Gargoyle
items.text: Oh, but perhaps my age hath eclipsed my wisdom. For I have thus far been an unwelcoming host. Allow me to brew you some tea.
She leaves with singular purpose and surprising speed.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: My aunt is a gentle soul. She came by here one year ago, not fearing the danger, saying she must take care of everyone left in the family.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: That old lump of stone that greeted us came here to take refuge with his brother after they were injured last year.
She hangs her head with resignation.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Only a small number of my kind dwell here. Many of us remain divided by the war.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Enjoy my aunt's hospitality. I shall go now to collect what you seek.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: I'll be here then.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Hold on.
She lets herself relax only a moment before noticing the stone-faced Gargoyles that look down at her from a dozen perches.
A thought crawls under her skin.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Hello?
She spins around in place, meeting the unblinking eyes of each statue, stopping on the figure of a young girl.
The girl's hands cover her face in a mournful pose—the silent tragedy of an endless moment of loss.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: This is ...
Why hath my cousin brought you here?
A voice calls out behind her, rigid and almost rude.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Huh?
A tall, gaunt monk stands in the courtyard.
You are not one of us. You are a bringer of war in our house of peace. What dost your Foundation seek from our quiet halls?
There's accusation in the gravelly tone of his voice.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: You misunderstand. The Foundation isn't bringing war. We're trying to end it.
This war is neither yours nor ours to end.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: What are you saying?
The monk falls silent, as if debating whether his next words are worth the effort.
His face contorts, becoming an exaggeration of self-righteousness.
It has come as a divine punishment for the faithless who have turned from God. Its end will come only with the extinction of civilization.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Sounds like you want everyone—humans and arcanists alike—to suffer and die.
You twist my words, knight. I do not seek this end—this path of suffering—out of hatred for humanity. No, I do so because I pray fervently for their deliverance.
But deliverance waits for the last edifices of this sinful world to crumble. When the faithless nations, as a fire consuming its last embers, burn themselves to ash.
Soon the artifices of modernity, their factories of war and death, will crumble, as Babel before them had; their lies of "advancement" and "revolution" dying with them.
We must return to the innocence of the past, as Nineveh did, heeding the word of God.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Enough, cousin.
The rebuke breaks his rhythm.
Sentinel steps between Marsha and Ladislas, forcing her cousin to take a step away.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Your prophecies have kept our guest from her tea.
Sentinel turns and hands Marsha a heavy canvas military bag.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Um!

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Are you able to lift it?

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: No problem. I can handle it.
Ladislas watches the exchange with abject curiosity.

items.speaker: Ladislas
items.text: Marianne, is she not of the very Foundation thou sayest lacketh the will to end this war? What fruitless endeavor dost thou now pursue?

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: She's my friend, Ladislas. I shall grant her the freedom to come and go from here as she wills.

items.speaker: Ladislas
items.text: But she is not a ...

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: It is my right to do this, is it not?

items.speaker: Ladislas
items.text: Yes.
He lowers his head without protest.
Sentinel turns from her kin back to Marsha, who has by now taken several steps away.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: You will find here all that I've collected since 1918; most useful to you may be a list of those in each military who have made contact with the Manus.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Take them from here to your Foundation and make of them what you will. I hope they will serve you better than they did me.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: I will. Thank you.
Marsha seems more than eager to retreat.
Aunt Madeleine stands at the foot of a stone pillar, tea in her hand, and nods in self-reproach.
The courtyard falls still.
Ladislas breaks his silence with a withering glare.

items.speaker: Ladislas
items.text: Cousin, why hast thou concerned thyself with the affairs of this sinful world? We are involved now at our peril.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Even if this war was, as you believe, a divine punishment, the people have suffered enough.

items.speaker: Ladislas
items.text: Have they? I see no sackcloth, only ashes!
He motions to the weeping girl tucked in the sanctuary niche.

items.speaker: Ladislas
items.text: Hast thou learned nothing from our dear Agnès?

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Leave her out of this.

items.speaker: Ladislas
items.text: It was she who prophesied this war ...
He drags up the memory with sharp intention.

items.speaker: Ladislas
items.text: And whose body turned to stone as it came to pass.

items.speaker: Ladislas
items.text: Was she not the closest of us all to the ear of our Lord? Then I can see only one reason for her sacrifice. It is a warning to us.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Tell me, if that is so, why God would choose such a warning?

items.speaker: Ladislas
items.text: Revelation and prophecy oft appear inscrutable to those that disbelieve them, until their truth is made manifest.
Ladislas's voice trembles, a practiced tension of humility and pride.

items.speaker: Ladislas
items.text: But I do believe, and I see clearly what thou hast not—that our Lord bids us to neither fight nor end this war.

items.speaker: Ladislas
items.text: Because it hath come as the next great deluge to sweep this sinful world away. Agnès will return to us again as our past innocence is found and rebuilt from their ruins.

items.speaker: Ladislas
items.text: But the faith must be preserved if it is to be rebuilt, and these labors will be the task of the faithful—of we, the Gargoyles.

items.speaker: Ladislas
items.text: I pray thee heed my words, cousin: Lay down thy sword of vengeance. Do not answer to the whispering demon in thy blood, nor stain thy soul already so burdened with sin!
He lets his words cling to his lips with solemn weight.
His cousin, however, has never been easy to preach to. She stiffens, sorrow and purpose welling in her eyes.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Guns, cannons, tanks, bombs ...

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: You do remember how these devices have destroyed our lives, do you not? Then surely you already know ...

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: That the innocence of the past does not simply lie buried for us to rebuild. It is dead and gone.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: If a stain on my soul is what it takes to end this war, then I shall not hesitate to stain it so.
Ladislas is stunned. He fights back tears and turns to face the altar. The light from the stained glass windows wreathes him like a mourner's cloak.

items.speaker: Ladislas
items.text: Hast thou forgotten our ancestral peril? Or the manifold names we have stricken from our line when they turned from the righteous path? The demon blood hath overtaken our kin before, as I fear it soon will overtake thee.

items.speaker: Ladislas
items.text: I do not wish to blot out thy name as well ... Marianne.
